bms_4168_0800343c.name: PendSV_Handler

bms_4168_0800343c.description: Vector-table entry for the PendSV system exception (exception number -2). The body is a bare return, so this build does no deferred work and no context switch in PendSV. Its priority, when configured, is written by NVIC_SetPriority into the SCB SHPR3 byte.

bms_4168_08003474.name: rcc_hclk_divide
bms_4168_08003474.summary: Divide a clock frequency by the AHB (HCLK) prescaler read from RCC_CFGR
bms_4168_08003474.description: Reads RCC.CFGR (0x40021008) and takes the HPRE field (bits 7:4) as a 4-byte-stride index into a 16-entry table in flash at 0x08010a54. Each table entry is the right-shift count for one AHB prescaler setting (0 for undivided, 1 for /2, 2 for /4, ... 9 for /512). The function returns its argument shifted right by that count, which is the input divided by the AHB prescaler. Used in clock-tree arithmetic to derive HCLK from SYSCLK; no writes and no side effects.

params.name: param_1
params.description: input frequency to divide, e.g. SYSCLK in Hz

returns.description: param_1 divided by the AHB prescaler

bms_4168_08003474.notes: Table contents are inferred from the STM32 HAL AHBPrescTable layout, not read from the image. The table is read at a 4-byte stride as decompiled; the element width is unverified.

bms_4168_08003494.name: rcc_pclk_divide
bms_4168_08003494.summary: Divide a clock frequency by the APB (PCLK) prescaler read from RCC_CFGR
bms_4168_08003494.description: Reads RCC.CFGR (0x40021008), masks it to 15 bits and takes bits 14:12 as the index of a 8-entry shift-count table at 0x08010a94 (4-byte stride), i.e. the APB prescaler selection. The function returns its argument shifted right by the selected count, which is the input divided by the APB prescaler. No writes and no side effects. Companion of rcc_hclk_divide.

params.name: param_1
params.description: input frequency to divide, e.g. HCLK in Hz

returns.description: param_1 divided by the APB prescaler

bms_4168_08003494.notes: The index uses CFGR bits 14:12. In the STM32G0 reference manual the APB prescaler PPRE field is at bits 10:8, so either the field position or the decompiled shift needs checking against the RM before the exact divider is trusted. Table location and element width are inferred the same way as in rcc_hclk_divide.

bms_4168_08003514.name: bms_u8_to_bcd
bms_4168_08003514.summary: Convert an 8-bit binary value to packed BCD
bms_4168_08003514.description: Converts a byte to packed BCD by repeatedly subtracting 10 and counting the tens (the subtraction is kept to 8 bits). The result is the ones digit in the low nibble and the tens count in the high nibble. Correct for inputs 0..159; above 159 the tens count exceeds 15 and is masked to 4 bits, so the result wraps. No globals, registers or memory are touched. Callers bms_4168_08002704 and bms_4168_080027a4 likely format a value for a byte-oriented protocol field.

returns.description: packed BCD: tens in bits 7:4, ones in bits 3:0

bms_4168_08003624.name: SVC_Handler

bms_4168_08003624.description: Vector-table entry for the SVCall system exception (exception number -5). The body is a bare return, so supervisor calls perform no work in this build. Its priority, when configured, is written by NVIC_SetPriority into the SCB SHPR2 byte (bits 31:30 of the word).

bms_4168_08003626.name: crc8_msb_compute
bms_4168_08003626.summary: CRC-8 over a byte buffer, MSB-first, init 0, polynomial supplied by the caller
bms_4168_08003626.description: Computes an 8-bit CRC over len bytes starting at data, with the polynomial passed in poly and an initial value of 0. Bytes are processed MSB first with no reflection and no final XOR. For each bit the CRC is shifted left and XORed with poly when the old bit 7 was set, then XORed with poly again when the data bit is set; this is the standard step crc = (crc << 1) ^ (((crc7 ^ data_bit) != 0) ? poly : 0). Common polynomials for this form are 0x07 (CRC-8/SMBus) and 0x31 (Dallas/Maxim); the caller's choice is not visible in this packet. Only general-purpose registers are used.
bms_4168_08003626.notes: The decompiler shows a void return, but the CRC accumulator is the only live value at exit, so the result is presumably returned in r0; this is unverified. The only caller in the packet is bms_4168_0800b7bc, which would confirm it.

bms_4168_0800366a.name: bms_empty_callback

It is most likely a no-op placeholder used as a default or unused hook in a handler or event table.
bms_4168_0800366a.notes: What the code does is certain; which table or event it is registered in is unknown.

bms_4168_08003700.name: bms_copy_bytes8
bms_4168_08003700.summary: Copy exactly 8 bytes from source to destination, unrolled
bms_4168_08003700.description: Copies 8 bytes from src to dst one byte at a time, fully unrolled, with no loop, no length argument and no overlap handling. The fixed size of 8 matches a classic CAN payload or a small 8-byte record; the data it moves is not identified in this packet. Several callers in the 4139 and 4168 builds use it, so it is a shared helper for small fixed-size copies.
bms_4168_08003700.notes: The 8-byte size is certain; the payload type is a guess.

bms_4168_08003724.name: NVIC_SetPriority
bms_4168_08003724.summary: CMSIS NVIC_SetPriority: set the 2-bit priority of an IRQ or system exception
bms_4168_08003724.description: CMSIS-style NVIC_SetPriority for the Cortex-M0+. The priority in param_2 is masked to 2 bits and placed in bits 7:6 of its byte lane (STM32G0 implements __NVIC_PRIO_BITS = 2). For a negative IRQn, meaning a system exception (SVCall -5, PendSV -2, SysTick -1), the byte is written into the SCB SHPR2/SHPR3 word at 0xE000ED1C through a read-modify-write that keeps the other three byte lanes. For IRQn >= 0 the byte goes into the NVIC IPR array at 0xE000E400 with the same read-modify-write. Caller bms_4168_0800a3e8 sets interrupt priorities.

params.name: param_1
params.description: IRQn: negative for system exceptions, otherwise device IRQ number

bms_4168_080038c8.name: bms_window_latch_narrow
bms_4168_080038c8.summary: Debounced latch for the narrow window (+8 < 40, +10 > 5); counts whole units while latched
bms_4168_080038c8.description: Per-sample update of a time-debounced hysteresis latch. param_1 is a sample record: byte +0 is the time step added per call, byte +1 is an enable (0 clears all state and returns param_2 unchanged), and signed 16-bit readings at +8 and +10 are tested against the window, which is in-window when +8 < 40 and +10 > 5. Inside the window with the latch clear, or outside the 3-unit hysteresis band (+8 > 37 or +10 < 8), the timer DAT_20000608 is reset. Otherwise the timer accumulates the step, and at 30 the latch DAT_20000601 is cleared; outside the window the timer accumulates to 30 and then sets the latch and clamps the timer to 30. While the latch is set, the sub-accumulator DAT_2000060a adds the step and each time it exceeds 9 it subtracts 10 and increments param_2, so the return value counts whole tens of step units spent latched.

params.name: param_1
params.description: sample record: +0 u8 step, +1 u8 enable, +8 s16 reading A (upper limit 40), +10 s16 reading B (lower limit 5)

params.name: param_2
params.description: running count in units of 10 step units, returned incremented

returns.description: param_2 plus whole tens of latched time accumulated in this call

bms_4168_080038c8.notes: Readings A and B are probably max and min pack temperatures in degrees C, since 5..40 is a typical charge window; this is inferred from the thresholds only. The latch semantics are read from the control flow and are high confidence; the physical meaning is medium. Sibling of bms_window_latch_wide with the same algorithm and a different window.

bms_4168_08003954.name: bms_window_latch_wide
bms_4168_08003954.summary: Debounced latch for the wide window (+8 < 55, +10 > -15); counts whole units while latched
bms_4168_08003954.description: Same algorithm as bms_window_latch_narrow with its own state: byte +0 is the time step, byte +1 the enable, and signed readings at +8 and +10 are tested against a wider window (in-window when +8 < 55 and +10 > -15). Hysteresis exits at +8 > 52 or +10 < -12, the latch threshold is 30 step units, and the state is held in DAT_20000600 (latch), DAT_20000604 (timer) and DAT_20000606 (sub-accumulator, carry at 10). Returns param_2 with whole tens of latched time added.

params.name: param_1
params.description: sample record: +0 u8 step, +1 u8 enable, +8 s16 reading A (upper limit 55), +10 s16 reading B (lower limit -15)

params.name: param_2
params.description: running count in units of 10 step units, returned incremented

returns.description: param_2 plus whole tens of latched time accumulated in this call

bms_4168_08003954.notes: The window limits suggest a discharge-type window (-15..55 C) while the narrow one suggests charge (5..40 C); the readings are inferred as temperatures from the limits only.

bms_4168_08004da4.name: crc16_usb_compute
bms_4168_08004da4.summary: Bitwise CRC-16, reflected poly 0x8005, init 0xFFFF, final complement
bms_4168_08004da4.description: Bitwise CRC-16 over len bytes starting at data. The register starts at 0xFFFF, each byte is XORed into its low half, and then 8 steps shift right and XOR 0xA001 (reflected 0x8005) whenever the LSB is set. The result is complemented (~crc & 0xFFFF). These parameters match CRC-16/USB. CRC-16/MODBUS uses the same polynomial and initial value without the final complement, so the caller's expected form must be checked before reusing it for Modbus frames. No globals, peripherals or memory writes.
bms_4168_08004da4.notes: Callers in the packet: bms_4139_08007108, bms_4168_08005128, bms_4168_08007c10, bms_4168_080106c8. Whether the CRC is CRC-16/USB or a custom variant is inferred from the constants; the frame it protects is not identified here.

bms_4168_08005ee4.name: bms_slot_table_find
bms_4168_08005ee4.summary: Find or allocate a 36-byte slot keyed by an 8-bit pair
bms_4168_08005ee4.description: Searches a table of 36-byte (0x24) records. param_1 points to a header whose pointer at +0 is the record array and whose u16 at +4 is the record count. Each record has key byte 0, key byte 1, and a state byte at +2 where 1 marks a free slot. With param_4 == 0 (strict mode) the function first returns 0 if the reversed pair (param_3, param_2) is in use, then returns the record keyed (param_2, param_3) if one exists, and otherwise the first free slot. With param_4 != 0 it skips the reversed check and returns the record keyed (param_2, param_3) or the first free slot. It returns a record pointer, or 0 when nothing matches and no slot is free.

params.name: param_1
params.description: table header: +0 record array pointer, +4 u16 record count

params.name: param_4
params.description: mode: 0 = strict (reject reversed pair), nonzero = lenient

returns.description: pointer to the matching or newly free record, or 0

bms_4168_08005ee4.notes: The table most likely maps a link between two 8-bit IDs to a slot; what the IDs are is not in this packet. The state value 1 = free is read from the loops and should be checked against the writers. The record stride 0x24 and the header layout are certain from the code.

bms_4168_080072ec.name: bms_tracking_filter_step
bms_4168_080072ec.summary: One step of a dead-band tracking filter that slews an estimate toward a measurement
bms_4168_080072ec.description: Moves the estimate DAT_20000eec one count toward the measurement DAT_20000ee8 with a dead-band accumulator. When the two differ, the step is the absolute difference masked to 20 bits and shifted right by 4, with a minimum of 5, signed toward the measurement, and it is added to the 16-bit accumulator DAT_200001f6. When the accumulator reaches 129 or more, the estimate is incremented and 128 is subtracted from the accumulator; when it reaches -129 or less, the estimate is decremented (clamped at 0) and 128 is added. Between those limits the estimate and accumulator are left alone, which is the dead band. No peripherals are touched.

returns.description: none; the state is in RAM globals

bms_4168_080072ec.notes: Globals: DAT_20000ee8 read-only measurement, DAT_20000eec estimate (read/write), DAT_200001f6 accumulator (16-bit signed). The 20-bit mask and >>4 suggest a high-resolution ADC or AFE reading, but the quantity (SOC, current, voltage) is a guess.

The meaning of the individual variables is not established. Caller bms_4139_080072e0.
bms_4139_08007360.notes: Probably the same logical function as bms_app_state_reset. Address correspondence inferred from matching writes: 0x20000112 to 0x200001aa, 0x20000113 to 0x200001ab, 0x20000114 to 0x200001ac, 0x20000818 to 0x20000904. The legacy build has no equivalents of 0x20000a53 and 0x20000b57, which the newer layout clears. Kept as a separate family because the address layouts differ.

bms_4168_08008d4c.name: bms_systick_base_set

That word is the base count multiplied by the busy-wait helpers bms_systick_wait_repeat and bms_systick_wait_scaled, which poll SysTick until the requested number of counts has elapsed. Callers bms_4168_080082f0 and bms_4168_080086d4 set it before they wait. No peripheral access.

bms_4168_08008d58.name: bms_systick_wait_repeat
bms_4168_08008d58.summary: Busy-wait param_1 times, each for DAT_20000688 * 1000 SysTick counts
bms_4168_08008d58.description: Runs param_1 repetitions of a busy-wait. Each repetition polls SysTick->VAL (0xE000E018) until the elapsed count reaches DAT_20000688 * 1000. Elapsed counts come from successive VAL reads: the down-counter difference is added directly, and when VAL has wrapped past the reload value SysTick->LOAD (0xE000E014) the reload is added first, so the wait works across reloads. The loop has no interrupts, sleep or timeout, so it blocks the CPU for the whole duration. The 1000 factor means DAT_20000688 is in thousands of SysTick counts.
bms_4168_08008d58.notes: Callers in the packet: bms_4168_080082bc, bms_4168_080082f0, bms_4168_0800aa5c, bms_4168_0800aae8, bms_4168_0800b314, bms_4168_0800b406, bms_4168_0800b57e. Real time per count depends on the SysTick clock source, which is not in this packet.

It is the main delay primitive for the timing-sensitive routines in this build; seven callers in the packet use it. The use is probably bit-timed serial signalling or AFE sequencing, which is a guess.
bms_4168_08008da0.notes: Callers in the packet: bms_4168_08009428, bms_4168_08009664, bms_4168_08009740, bms_4168_0800982c, bms_4168_080098f0, bms_4168_0800997c, bms_4168_08009a0c. The loop compares the 32-bit target with a 32-bit accumulator, so very large multipliers wrap.

bms_4168_08009414.description: Writes 0x20 to GPIOA.BRR (0x50000028), which resets PA5 atomically. It is the reset half of gpio_pa5_set. The only caller in the packet is bms_4168_0800b8ac. The pin's function is not established.

bms_4168_0800941e.name: gpio_pa5_set
bms_4168_0800941e.summary: Drive GPIOA pin 5 high through BSRR
bms_4168_0800941e.description: Writes 0x20 to GPIOA.BSRR (0x50000018), which sets PA5 atomically. It is the set half of gpio_pa5_reset. The only caller in the packet is bms_4168_0800b8ac.
